findings.title: Team admin/owner check uses && so team admins are rejected
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`. `isTeamAdmin` already returns true for both ADMIN and OWNER roles, so ANDing it with `isTeamOwner` reduces the check to "is owner". A team ADMIN who is not the organizer or an attendee gets FORBIDDEN, even though the variable name and intent say admins are allowed. Use `||`, or call `isTeamAdmin` alone.

findings.title: Calendar update runs with the caller's credentials instead of the organizer's
findings.body: The `EventManager` is built from `ctx.user` and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`. The handler explicitly allows team owners and booking attendees, who are not the organizer, to call it. In those cases the booking's calendar and video references, which belong to the organizer's credentials, are updated with the wrong user's credentials. The update then fails, or touches the wrong account. The handler already loads `booking.user` with `credentials`, but never uses them. The EventManager should be built from the booking organizer's user and credentials.

findings.title: Calendar update failure after DB write leaves state inconsistent and blocks retry
findings.body: New attendees are committed with `prisma.booking.update` before `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` runs, and that call is not wrapped in try/catch. If the calendar or video provider call throws, the client gets an error, but the guests are already saved. Because of the throw, no emails are sent and the external calendar is not updated. If the user retries, the existing-attendee filter removes those guests and the handler throws "emails_must_be_unique_valid". The guests stay in the DB and are never notified.

findings.title: Case-sensitive comparisons bypass blacklist and allow duplicate attendees
findings.body: `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` entries are lowercased, but `guest` is compared without lowercasing. `Bad@Example.com` therefore passes the blacklist check. The existing-attendee check `guest === attendee.email` is also case-sensitive, so `Foo@x.com` can be added next to an existing `foo@x.com`. Normalize guest emails (trim and lowercase) before both comparisons.

findings.title: Unbounded, non-unique guest array accepted server-side
findings.body: `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no `.max()` and no uniqueness refinement. Uniqueness is only checked in the client dialog. Any authenticated attendee or organizer can call the endpoint directly with thousands of addresses, or with the same address repeated. That creates many or duplicate Attendee rows via `createMany` and makes the server send an email to each address in the organizer's name, which is a spam vector. Add a reasonable max and dedupe or reject duplicates on the server.

findings.title: Any attendee can add arbitrary guests regardless of event-type guest settings or booking status
findings.body: Any logged-in user whose email matches an attendee is allowed to add guests. The handler does not check whether the event type disables or hides the guests booking field. It also does not check booking status, so cancelled, rejected or past bookings are accepted. This lets attendees bypass host-configured restrictions and trigger organizer-branded emails and calendar invites to arbitrary addresses.

findings.title: Emails classified using raw input instead of filtered new guests
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` receives the unfiltered input list. If the input contains an email that was already an attendee (filtered out of `uniqueGuests`), that existing attendee is treated as a new guest. They get a fresh "booking scheduled" email instead of the "guests added" notice. Pass `uniqueGuests`. The catch block also discards `err`, so failures are hard to diagnose.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores disableStandardEmails event-type settings
findings.body: Every other booking email sender takes `eventTypeMetadata` and skips host or attendee emails when `disableStandardEmails.all.host` or `.attendee` is set. `sendAddGuestsEmails` has no such parameter or check, and the handler does not pass metadata. Organizations that turned off standard emails, for example to use their own workflows, will still get organizer and attendee emails whenever guests are added.

findings.title: Error toast fallback is unreachable and can show 'undefined: ...'
findings.body: `message` is a template string and is always truthy, so `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` never uses the fallback. When `err.data?.code` is undefined, for example on network or non-TRPC errors, the toast reads "undefined: <message>".

findings.title: Validation error state is not reset on success or on dismiss
findings.body: `isInvalidEmail` is set to true on a failed validation, but nothing resets it after a successful add, after the user fixes the input, or when the dialog is closed via overlay or Escape (`onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}`). Only the Cancel button resets it. On reopening, the dialog still shows "Emails must be unique and valid" and may also keep stale email values.

findings.title: New mutation has no tests
findings.body: The new handler covers permission checks, filtering, DB writes, calendar updates and email sending, but the PR adds no unit or e2e tests. Several of the bugs above (admin check, case handling, credentials used) would have been caught by basic coverage of these paths.
